decor.name: the Corn Exchange price board
decor.text: BREAD: DEAR. FLOUR: DEARER. GRAIN: ASK. QUESTIONS: NOT TAKEN.

decor.name: a sign
decor.text: NO BUNTING BEYOND THIS POINT. BY ORDER OF THE ASSEMBLY COMMITTEE (DECORATIONS SUB-COMMITTEE).

decor.name: a grain cart
decor.text: A granary cart with one wheel off, which is how it gets out of processions.

decor.name: a notice by the palace gate
decor.text: THE CENTENNIAL ASSEMBLY. DELEGATIONS BY THE FRONT. TRADES BY THE BACK. PIGS NOT AT ALL.

decor.name: the old elm
decor.text: Old, dry and leaning over the yard wall. The pigeons in it have opinions about everybody.

decor.name: a lamp post
decor.text: A lamp post, freshly painted for the Assembly and already leant on.

decor.name: a lamp post
decor.text: A lamp post, freshly painted for the Assembly and already leant on.

decor.name: a market stall
decor.text: A stall selling Assembly souvenirs: commemorative mugs with the King's face on, the face slightly wrong.

decor.name: the statue of Good King Bertram
decor.text: Good King Bertram the Moderately Wise, in bronze, with a pigeon on his head. The pigeon looks more regal.

decor.name: the town well
decor.text: The town well. A sign says NO WISHING, BY ORDER: it was causing a shortage of pennies.

decor.name: the stocks
decor.text: The stocks, freshly painted for the Assembly. A sign on them says RESERVED.

decor.name: a cabbage cart
decor.text: A cart of cabbages at Assembly prices. The cabbages are the bargain; the cart is also for sale, and so, if you ask nicely, is the donkey.

decor.name: crates
decor.text: Crates marked FRAGILE, which the porters take as a challenge.

decor.name: the wharf crane
decor.text: A treadwheel crane. A sign on the wheel says NO HAMSTERS.

regions.name: the yard behind the King's Granary
regions.label: Step into the granary yard
regions.lockedAfter: The yard's been locked up for the Assembly, and the dead-cart has been. Somebody has tied a ribbon on the padlock. You can see in over the wall, which is something.
regions.description: A cobbled yard swept bare for the Assembly, smelling of wet grain, pigeons and river mud.

regions.name: the tally loft
regions.description: Up under the granary roof: the tally desk, the grain stacks, and the Royal Granary Roll on its chain.

regions.name: the downriver end of the wharves
regions.label: Go along to the Heron
regions.description: Where the wharf lamps give out, and the Heron's hoist creaks over the water.

regions.name: the palace
regions.shut: The guards at the gate cross their halberds with the air of men who have been waiting all week to do it. The palace is shut to anyone without business.
regions.description: King Aldren's palace on the rise: gilt, tapestries and a great deal of new bunting, in a winter when bread is dear.

regions.name: Palace Street
regions.description: The procession route from the palace gate down to the square, bunting on every rope that will hold it.

regions.name: the granary lane
regions.description: The lane behind the King's Granary: porters, pigeons and, as far as the sign, bunting.

regions.name: the watch house
regions.description: The watch house. Everyone is out lining the procession route; a note on the door says so.

regions.name: the cart shed
regions.description: An open-fronted shed with a cart in it that has seen better wheels.

regions.name: the porters' lodgings
regions.description: Where the granary porters sleep, in shifts, in the same beds.

regions.name: the King's Granary
regions.description: The King's Granary: brick, timber and padlocks, and the palace's grain inside, what there is of it.

regions.name: Granary Street
regions.description: The street down from the granary quarter to the market square.

regions.name: Pudding Lane
regions.description: An alley behind the granary that smells of neither pudding nor anything you'd want in one.

regions.name: the market square
regions.description: Stalls, bunting, sweepers, delegations' servants everywhere, and bread dearer than last week.

regions.name: the Corn Exchange
regions.description: Where the grain factors trade, post prices and keep the wagon lists. Factors only.

regions.name: Cheap Alley
regions.description: A side alley where everything is cheap except the advice.

regions.name: Bank Street
regions.description: The street along the top of the bank, with the river below and the smell of it everywhere.

regions.name: the Drowned Rat's door
regions.shut: The Drowned Rat's door is shut. A board nailed to it says: OPENS AT DUSK. NO CREDIT. NO WATCH ON DUTY. N. QUILL.
regions.description: A low, heavy door in the bank, three steps down from the landing, with the din of the Rat behind it.

regions.name: the river stairs
regions.description: Worn, wet steps down the bank to the wharves. Nobody has ever counted the same number twice. Halfway down, the Drowned Rat's door.

regions.name: the wharves
regions.description: Boards, bollards, crates and the river slapping underneath. Porters wait for work with their hooks.

regions.name: the Heron warehouse
regions.description: A tall, tarred warehouse half on the wharf and half on piles, under a painted heron.

regions.name: the river
regions.description: Brown, fast and freezing. What goes in comes out at the sea, or doesn't.

people.name: a palace guard
people.text: A palace guard in a breastplate polished for the Assembly. He has been told to look stern and is giving it everything.

people.name: a palace guard
people.text: The other palace guard, who is looking stern slightly better than the first and knows it.

people.name: pigeons
people.text: Pigeons, watching the bunting go up with professional interest.

people.name: a sweeper
people.text: A sweeper. 'Assembly tomorrow. Sweep it all up so they can drop it all again tomorrow. That's civic pride, that is.'

people.name: a man up a ladder
people.text: A man up a ladder with an armful of bunting and the expression of someone who has run out of rope and patience at the same time.

people.name: a goose
people.text: A goose. It belongs to nobody and fears nothing. It looks at you as if you owe it money.

people.name: a pie-seller
people.text: A pie-seller. 'Assembly pies! Commemorative! Mostly pork!' You decide not to ask about the rest.

people.name: a porter
people.text: A granary porter with a sack on his shoulder. 'Shocking business, the clerk. Shocking. Mind your back.'

people.name: a woman haggling over cabbages
people.text: 'How much? For a cabbage? I could buy a goose for that.' Somewhere behind you, the goose takes this personally.

people.name: an official with a clipboard
people.text: An official of the Assembly Committee (Decorations Sub-Committee), measuring the bunting with a ruler. 'Seven inches between flags. SEVEN. Is that so very hard?'

people.name: a boy selling programmes
people.text: 'Programme! Order of procession! The Purveyor's grain cart! The King's speech!' Quieter: 'It's the same as last century's. They just change the date.'

people.name: a delegation's servant
people.text: A Saltmere servant in salt-gull livery, haggling for bread and losing. 'This is what you charge for a loaf?' 'It's the Assembly, love.'

people.name: a stallholder
people.text: A stallholder selling commemorative mugs with the King's face on, the face slightly wrong. 'Two for a penny. Three for a penny if you take the one with the nose.'

people.name: a lamplighter
people.text: A lamplighter with a long pole and a short temper. 'Lamps at dusk, lamps at dusk. Nobody ever says thank you to a lamplighter.' Thank you. 'Don't push it.'

people.name: porters going down to the Rat
people.text: Big men going down the river stairs, paid off early and off to drink it, most of them bandaged somewhere. It's the docks.

people.name: a barge lantern
people.text: A lantern on a moored barge, swinging, making the dark darker everywhere else.

people.name: a barge lantern
people.text: A lantern on a moored barge, swinging, making the dark darker everywhere else.

people.name: a watchman's brazier
people.text: A brazier glowing outside the Heron's land door, at the very end of the wharf where the lamps give out.

people.name: an eel-seller packing up
people.text: An eel-seller packing up. 'Last eels! Lively ones!' They are, alarmingly.

people.name: the crowd
people.text: The crowd, out early for the procession, holding flags, children and opinions.

people.name: the Purveyor's grain cart
people.text: The Royal Purveyor's grain cart, garlanded, waiting to walk fourth in the procession 'for the people's confidence'. It is mostly garland.

people.name: a Nine Furrows banner-bearer
people.text: A Nine Furrows delegate under a wheat-sheaf banner, discussing the weather with the authority of someone whose people make it.

people.name: a Kläggenheim axeman
people.text: A Kläggenheim delegate with a ceremonial axe, which he assures you is ceremonial. He has assured several people. It is quite sharp.
